Do you see the gods of the desire realm, up to the Akanishtha Heaven, raining down fragrant flowers throughout the Buddha-lands, or do you not? Ānanda replied: Yes, indeed, I have seen them.
[The Kind One] Bodhisattva Maitreya.

[Do you hear the great voice of Amitābha Buddha proclaiming throughout all worlds and transforming sentient beings? Ānanda replied: Yes, indeed, I have heard it. The Buddha said: Do you see the host of pure practitioners in that land, roaming and dwelling in the sky with their palaces following after them; without obstruction, going everywhere throughout the ten directions to make offerings to the Buddhas? And do you see them recollecting the Buddha without interruption?]

The World-Honored One asked further: Do you hear the great voice of Amitābha Buddha reaching throughout all worlds and teaching sentient beings, or do you not? Ānanda replied: Yes, indeed, I have heard it. The World-Honored One asked further: Do you see the host of pure practitioners in that land (the Land of Utmost Bliss), roaming and dwelling (coming forth and abiding) in the sky with their palaces following after them; without obstruction, going everywhere throughout the ten directions to make offerings to the Buddhas, or do you not? And do you see them recollecting the Buddha without interruption (reciting the Buddha's name without interruption by deluded thoughts), or do you not?
The Sutra of Immeasurable Life as Spoken by the Buddha (the Wei translation) says:
“Have you also heard the great voice of Amitayus Buddha proclaiming throughout all worlds
(reaching throughout all worlds)
and transforming sentient beings? Ānanda replied: Yes, indeed, I have heard it.”

[Moreover, there are many birds dwelling in the sky who utter all kinds of sounds; all are transformations wrought by the Buddha — do you see them all? Maitreya replied: As the Buddha has said, I see each and every one.]

Moreover, there are many birds dwelling in the sky who utter all kinds of sounds; all are transformations wrought by the Buddha — do you all see them? Bodhisattva Maitreya replied: As the Buddha has said, I see each and every one.
Transformation-wrought] Manifested through spiritual power. The Lotus Sutra says:

“Then Bodhisattva Wondrous Sound, without rising from his seat and without stirring his body, entered samādhi. By the power of that samādhi, on Mount Gridhrakuta, not far from the Dharma seat, he wrought eighty-four thousand lotuses of manifold treasures.”

[The Buddha said to Maitreya: Among the people of that land, some are womb-born — do you see them too? Maitreya replied: World-Honored One, I see the people of the Land of Utmost Bliss who dwell in the flower-womb, like the gods of the Yama Heaven dwelling in their palaces. And I see sentient beings seated cross-legged
jiā
fū)
within the lotus, born by transformation of themselves, emerging in an instant. For what reason are the people of that land some womb-born and some transformation-born?]

The Buddha told Bodhisattva Maitreya: Do you also see that among the people of the Land of Utmost Bliss some are womb-born? Bodhisattva Maitreya replied: World-Honored One, I see those of the Land of Utmost Bliss who dwell in the flower-womb, like beings in the Yama Heaven dwelling in their palaces. And I see sentient beings seated cross-legged within the lotus, born by transformation of themselves, emerging in an instant. For what reason are the people of that land (the Land of Utmost Bliss) some womb-born and some transformation-born?
[Cross-legged sitting (
jiā
fū)]

Placing the two feet crossed over the left and right thighs is called “full cross-legged sitting.” Placing only the left foot over the right thigh, or only the right foot over the left thigh, is called “half cross-legged sitting.”
Emerging in an instant
] The Sutra of the Assembly of Immeasurable Life (the Tang translation) says:

“If there are sentient beings who cut off doubt and regret, accumulate roots of virtue, seek the Buddha's wisdom, even unto vast and great wisdom, and have faith in their own roots of virtue, such a person, seated cross-legged within the lotus, is suddenly born by transformation, emerging in an instant.”

blocks.text: 40. The Border Region and the City of Doubt

inline.s: [The Buddha said to the Kind One: If there are sentient beings who cultivate all merits with a doubting mind and vow to be born in that land, yet do not understand the Buddha's wisdom, the inconceivable wisdom, the inexpressible wisdom, the vast wisdom of the Great Vehicle, the unequaled and unrivaled supreme wisdom, and toward these wisdoms harbor doubt and do not believe — but still believe in offense and merit, cultivate the roots of goodness, and vow to be born in that land, then:]

The Buddha said to Bodhisattva Maitreya: If there are sentient beings who cultivate all merits with a doubting mind and vow to be born in the Western Land of Utmost Bliss, yet cannot believe in and understand the Buddha's wisdom, the inconceivable wisdom, the inexpressible wisdom, the vast wisdom of the Great Vehicle, the unequaled and unrivaled supreme wisdom, and toward these sage wisdoms harbor doubt and do not believe — but still believe in the karmic retribution of offense and merit, and cultivate the roots of goodness and vow to be born in that land, then:

[Again there are sentient beings who accumulate roots of virtue and seek the Buddha's wisdom, the universal wisdom, the unequaled wisdom, the majestic and vast inconceivable wisdom, yet cannot give rise to faith in their own roots of virtue.]

Again there are sentient beings who accumulate roots of virtue and seek the Buddha's wisdom, the universal wisdom, the unequaled wisdom, the majestic and vast inconceivable wisdom, yet cannot give rise to faith in their own roots of virtue.

[Therefore, in being born in a pure Buddha-land, their will wavers and they have nothing on which to take their stand. Yet they still continue reciting without cease and bind up their good vows as the foundation, and so they too attain rebirth.]

The two kinds of people above do not believe in the Buddha's wisdom, or do not believe in their own roots of virtue; therefore, when they are born in the Western Land of Utmost Bliss, their will wavers and they have nothing on which to take their stand. But they still recite the Buddha's name without cease and bind up their good vows as the foundation, and so they too attain rebirth.

[Such persons, for this reason, though born in that land, cannot come before Amitayus, but stop at the border of the Buddha-land, in a seven-jewel city. The Buddha does not make them so; it is what their own bodily actions have done, and their own minds that tend there. There are also jewel-ponds and lotuses, in which they spontaneously receive a body. Their food and drink and their happiness are as in the Trayastrimsa Heaven.]
They,

for this reason, though born in the Western Land of Utmost Bliss, cannot come before the Buddha, but stop in the seven-jewel city at the border of the Buddha-land. It is not Amitābha Buddha who causes them to be born there (in the border region and the city of doubt); rather, it is what their own bodily actions have done, what their own minds have manifested, and so they are naturally born there. There too are jewel-ponds and lotuses, and within the lotus they spontaneously receive a body. Their food, drink, and happiness are as in the palace of the Trayastrimsa Heaven.
[The Buddha does not make them so; it is what their own bodily actions have done, and their own minds that tend there] The Avatamsaka Sutra says:
“One should contemplate the nature of the Dharma-realm: all is made by mind alone.”

Because “when the mind arises, all dharmas arise,” hells, heavens, pure lands, and Buddha-lands are all manifested by one's own mind. Where the body tends is entirely drawn along by one's own thoughts. Hence it is said, “the mind itself tends there.” [Spontaneously receive a body] Therefore it is not birth from a mother's womb in the world.
The Sutra of Amitābha Buddha, the Samyaksambuddha Sarvabuddha-rajasamudra-veda-parama-hridaya (the Wu translation) says:

“When such a person's lifespan comes to its end, he is at once reborn in the land of Amitābha Buddha. He cannot come before Amitābha Buddha, but on the way he sees the border of the land of Amitābha Buddha and a spontaneous seven-jewel city, and his mind is filled with great joy, and he stops within that city. There, in the seven-jewel water-ponds, he is born by transformation within a lotus, and receiving a body, he spontaneously grows to maturity within the city.”
[As in the Trayastrimsa Heaven] The Sutra of Immeasurable Life as Spoken by the Buddha (the Wei translation) says:

“‘Among the people of that land some are womb-born — do you see them too?’ He replied: ‘I have seen them. Those who are womb-born dwell in palaces of a hundred yojanas, or five hundred yojanas, and each within them experiences all manner of happiness, as in the Trayastrimsa Heaven; all is spontaneous.’”

[But they dwell in the flower-womb and cannot come forth. For five hundred years they cannot see the Buddha, cannot hear the sutras and Dharma, and cannot see the bodhisattvas, sravakas, and assembly of sages. Such persons' wisdom is unclear, they know few sutras, their minds do not open and understand, and their hearts know no delight. Therefore, in that land, they are called womb-born.]

But they dwell in the flower-womb and cannot come forth. For five hundred years they cannot see the Buddha, cannot hear the sutras and Dharma, and cannot see the bodhisattvas, sravakas, and assembly of sages. Such persons' wisdom is unclear, they know few sutras, their minds do not open and understand, and their hearts know no delight. This is what is meant by womb-birth.

[If there are sentient beings who clearly believe in the Buddha's wisdom, even unto the supreme wisdom, who cut off doubt and believe in their own roots of virtue, perform all merits, and with utmost sincerity dedicate them, they all sit cross-legged within the lotuses of the seven-jewel ponds, born by transformation of themselves, emerging in an instant, their bodily marks radiant, their wisdom and merits equal to those of the bodhisattvas, fully accomplished.]

If there are sentient beings who firmly believe in the Buddha's wisdom, even unto the supreme wisdom, who cut off doubt and also believe in their own roots of virtue, perform all merits, and with utmost sincerity dedicate them, they all are born by transformation of themselves within the lotuses of the jewel-ponds of the Buddha, sitting cross-legged, emerging in an instant. In but a moment, their bodily marks are radiant and their wisdom and merits equal those of the bodhisattvas, fully accomplished.

[Maitreya, you should know that those born by transformation do so because their wisdom is superior. Those who are womb-born, for five hundred years, do not see the Three Jewels, do not know the bodhisattva's rule of conduct, cannot cultivate merits, and have no means to serve Amitābha Buddha. You should know that such persons, in former lives, had no wisdom — this is what doubt brought about.]

Maitreya, you should know that those born by transformation do so because their wisdom surpasses that of the womb-born. Those who are womb-born, for five hundred years, do not see the Three Jewels (they do not see Amitābha Buddha, do not hear the sutras and Dharma, and do not see the bodhisattvas, sravakas, and assembly of sages), do not know the bodhisattva's methods of practice, cannot cultivate merits, and have no means to serve Amitābha Buddha. You should know that such persons, in a former life (the life before their rebirth), had no wisdom — this is what doubt brought about.

blocks.text: 41. When Doubt Is Ended, One Sees the Buddha

inline.s: [Suppose a wheel-turning sage king had a seven-jewel prison, and a prince had committed an offense and was shut up within it. Its storied towers and splendid
(qǐ)

halls, its jeweled canopies and golden couches, its railings, windows, couches, and seats, were all adorned with rare and wondrous treasures. His food and clothing were as a wheel-turning king's, yet his two feet were bound with golden chains. Would the little princes take delight in this?]

Suppose a wheel-turning sage king had a seven-jewel prison, and a prince had committed an offense and was shut up within it. There too were storied towers and splendid halls, jeweled canopies and golden couches, railings, windows, couches, and seats, all adorned with rare and wondrous treasures. His food and clothing were as a wheel-turning sage king's, but his two feet were bound with golden chains. Would the little princes shut in that prison take delight in such a life?
[Splendid (qǐ) halls] Magnificent palaces.

[Maitreya replied: No, World-Honored One. While thus imprisoned, their minds are not at ease, and they seek only by every kind of means to gain release. Though they beg the close ministers, their wish is never fulfilled. Only when the wheel-turning king is pleased do they gain liberation.]

Bodhisattva Maitreya said to the Buddha: No, World-Honored One! While thus imprisoned, their minds are not at ease, and they seek only by every kind of means to gain release. Though they beg the close ministers, their wish is never fulfilled. Only when the wheel-turning king is pleased do they gain liberation.
[Imprisoned (zhí)] Confined. [Close ministers] The ministers who are near and dear to a ruler's side.

[The Buddha said to Maitreya: These sentient beings are likewise so. If there are those who fall into doubt and regret and seek the Buddha's wisdom, even unto vast and great wisdom, yet cannot give rise to faith in their own roots of virtue — because they hear the Buddha's name and give rise to faith, though they are born in that land, they cannot emerge from within the lotus.]

The Buddha said to Bodhisattva Maitreya: The womb-born sentient beings are likewise so. If, in seeking the Buddha's wisdom, even unto vast and great wisdom, they fall into doubt and regret; or if they cannot believe in their own roots of virtue — because they hear the Buddha's name and give rise to faith, though they are born in the Western Land of Utmost Bliss, they remain within the lotus womb of the border region and the city of doubt, and cannot come forth.

[Where they are, in the flower-womb, it seems to them a garden or a palace. Why is that? Because within it all is pure, free of every defilement and evil. Yet for five hundred years they do not see the Three Jewels, cannot make offerings or render service to the Buddhas, and are far removed from all supreme roots of virtue. They take this as suffering and give rise to no delight.]

Dwelling in the lotus womb of the border region and the city of doubt, they too feel it to be like a garden or a palace. Why is that? Because that place is pure, free of every defilement and evil. Yet for five hundred years they do not see the Three Jewels (they do not see Amitābha Buddha, do not hear the sutras and Dharma, and do not see the bodhisattvas, sravakas, and assembly of sages), cannot make offerings or render service to the Buddhas, and are far removed from all supreme roots of virtue. They take this as suffering and give rise to no delight.

[If such sentient beings recognize the root of their offense, deeply repent and reproach themselves, and seek to leave that place, then when the faults of their former lives are utterly exhausted, they at last come forth. They at once gain the way to come before Amitayus and hear the sutras and Dharma. In time they too will open their minds and rejoice, and will also be able to make offerings everywhere to countless, immeasurable Buddhas and cultivate all merits.]

If such sentient beings recognize where the root of their offense lies, deeply repent and correct themselves, and seek to leave the border region and the city of doubt, then when the faults of doubt from their former lives are utterly repented and purified, they are able to come forth from the lotus womb. They at once gain the way to come before Amitābha Buddha, hear the sutras and Dharma. In time they too will open their minds and rejoice, and will also be able to make offerings everywhere to countless, immeasurable Buddhas and cultivate all merits.
[You, Ajita, should know that doubt brings great harm to the bodhisattvas and is the loss of great benefit. Therefore you should clearly believe in the Buddhas' supreme wisdom.]
Maitreya, you should know that doubt brings great harm to the bodhisattvas and is the loss of great benefit. Therefore you should firmly believe in the Buddhas' supreme wisdom.
[Ajita] The courtesy name of Bodhisattva Maitreya.

[The Kind One replied: How is it that some sentient beings in this world, though they too cultivate goodness, do not seek rebirth? The Buddha said to the Kind One: Such sentient beings have shallow and slight wisdom. Discriminating, they judge the Western land to be inferior to the heavens, and so take no delight in it and do not seek rebirth there. The Kind One replied: Such sentient beings make false and deluded discriminations. If they do not seek the Buddha-land, how shall they escape the round of rebirth?]

Bodhisattva Maitreya replied: Why is it that in this world there is still a class of sentient beings who, though they too cultivate goodness, do not seek rebirth in the Western Land of Utmost Bliss? The Buddha said to Maitreya: Such sentient beings have shallow and slight wisdom. Discriminating, they judge the Western Land of Utmost Bliss to lack the desires and pleasures of the heavens, and so they take no delight in it and do not seek rebirth in the Western Land of Utmost Bliss. Bodhisattva Maitreya replied: Such sentient beings make false and deluded discriminations. If they do not seek rebirth in the Western Land of Utmost Bliss, how shall they escape the round of rebirth?

[If they do not seek the Buddha-land, how shall they escape the round of rebirth?] If they do not seek rebirth in the Western Land of Utmost Bliss, how shall they escape the round of rebirth? Though gods and humans have desires and pleasures, once their merit is spent and their lives end, they go on revolving within the six paths.

[The Buddha said: The roots of virtue planted by such beings cannot transcend marks; they do not seek the Buddha's wisdom, but cling deeply to worldly pleasures and to human blessings. Though they cultivate merit, they seek the fruit of gods and humans. When the reward comes, they have all abundance, yet they cannot escape the prison of the three realms. Even should parents, wives and children, and kin of both sexes wish to save and deliver them, the king of karma, wrong view, is not yet renounced, and they forever dwell in the round of rebirth, never at ease.]

The Buddha said: The roots of virtue planted by such sentient beings cannot transcend marks; they do not seek the Buddha's wisdom, but cling deeply to worldly pleasures and to human blessings. Though they cultivate merit, they seek the fruit of gods and humans. When the reward comes, they have all abundance, yet they cannot escape the prison of the three realms; when their merit is spent they fall back, and the harm to come is endless. After their lives end, even should parents, wives, children, and kin of both sexes cultivate the Dharma and recite the sutras, wishing to save and deliver them, yet because the king of karma, wrong view, is not yet renounced and they give rise to no right faith, they forever dwell in the round of rebirth, never at ease.
[The king of karma, wrong view] Because

of wrong view they give rise to no right faith, and so this wrong view is truly the king of all evil karma. Hence it is said, “the king of karma, wrong view.” [When merit is spent they fall back, and the harm to come is endless] This is what is commonly called “the grievance of three lifetimes.” [The grievance of three lifetimes] Because one cultivates in this life, in the next life one enjoys the reward of blessing, and so relying on that blessing one does evil, and this brings about one's fall in the life after that (the third lifetime). Even when the karma of hell is dissolved, one is again reborn as a hungry ghost or an animal, and to regain a human body is hard beyond hard! Therefore the World-Honored One asked Ānanda, holding up earth in his hand: “Is there more earth in my hand, or more in the great earth?” Ānanda replied: “There is more earth in the great earth.” The Buddha said: “Those who gain a human body are like the earth in my hand; those who lose a human body are like the earth of the great earth.” Hence, “through ten thousand kalpas and a thousand lives, not one person finds a refuge”! Therefore, if a practitioner does not end birth and death in this life, then after three lifetimes suffering and evil retribution are endless, and so it is called “the grievance of three lifetimes.” (See the article
The Grievance of Three Lifetimes

[You see the foolish, who plant no roots of virtue, but by worldly cleverness and glib argument increase their wrong minds. How shall they escape the great calamity of birth and death? Again there are sentient beings who, though they plant roots of virtue and make a great field of blessing, grasp at marks and discriminate, with deep and heavy emotional attachment. Seeking to escape the round of rebirth, they can never attain it.]

You see those foolish people, who plant no roots of virtue, but by worldly cleverness and glib argument increase their wrong minds. How can they escape the great calamity of birth and death? Again there are sentient beings who, though they plant roots of virtue and make a great field of blessing, yet grasp at marks and discriminate, with deep and heavy emotional attachment. In this way they seek to escape the round of rebirth, and can never attain it.
[Worldly cleverness and glib argument]
Worldly cleverness is the petty cleverness of ordinary worldly people; glib argument is using the petty cleverness of ordinary people to argue over right and wrong.

[If with the wisdom of no-marks one plants the roots of every virtue, with body and mind pure and far removed from discrimination, seeking birth in the pure land and tending toward the Buddha's bodhi, one shall be born in the Buddha-land and attain liberation forever.]

If with the wisdom of no-marks one plants the roots of every virtue, with body and mind pure and far removed from discrimination, seeking birth in the Western Land of Utmost Bliss and tending toward the Buddha's bodhi, then one will certainly attain rebirth in the Western Land of Utmost Bliss and attain liberation forever.

[Bodhisattva Maitreya said to the Buddha: In this Sahā world and in all the Buddha-lands, how many are the non-retrogressing bodhisattvas who shall be born in the Land of Utmost Bliss? The Buddha said to Maitreya: In this world there are seven hundred and twenty koṭis of bodhisattvas who have already made offerings to countless Buddhas and planted the roots of every virtue, and they shall be born in that land. As for the bodhisattvas of small practice who cultivate merits and shall attain rebirth, their number cannot be reckoned.]

Bodhisattva Maitreya said to the Buddha: In this Sahā world and in all the Buddha-lands, how many are the non-retrogressing bodhisattvas who shall be born in the Land of Utmost Bliss? The Buddha said to Bodhisattva Maitreya: In this Sahā world there are seven hundred and twenty koṭis of non-retrogressing bodhisattvas who have already made offerings to countless Buddhas and planted the roots of every virtue, and they shall be born in the Western Land of Utmost Bliss. As for the bodhisattvas of small practice who cultivate merits and shall attain rebirth, their number cannot be reckoned.

[The Sahā world] The word “Sahā” originally referred to the Jambudvipa in which we dwell, and in later ages it came to mean the three-thousand-great-thousand world taught by Śākyamuni Buddha, so that the whole of the hundred koṭis of Sumeru-worlds is called Sahā, and Śākyamuni is taken as the original teacher of the Sahā world. “The Sahā world” in this passage means precisely the three-thousand-great-thousand world taught by Śākyamuni Buddha. [Bodhisattvas of small practice] Bodhisattvas who have not yet reached the stage of non-retrogression.

[Not only the bodhisattvas of my own land are born in that land; in the Buddha-lands of other directions it is likewise so. From the Buddha-land of Far-Shining Radiance, eighteen nayutas of bodhisattva-mahasattvas are born in that land. In the northeast, in the Buddha-land of Store of Treasures, ninety koṭis of non-retrogressing bodhisattvas shall be born in that land. From the Buddha-lands of Immeasurable Sound, of Light, of Dragon Gods, of Victorious Power, of the Lion, of Freedom from Dust, of Foremost Virtue, of the Humane King, and of Flower Banner, the non-retrogressing bodhisattvas who shall attain rebirth number some tens or hundreds of koṭis, some hundreds of thousands of koṭis, even unto ten thousand koṭis.]

Not only the bodhisattvas of my own Buddha-land are born in the Western Land of Utmost Bliss; in the Buddha-lands of other directions it is likewise so. From the Buddha-land of Far-Shining Radiance, eighteen koṭis of koṭis of great bodhisattvas are born in the Western Land of Utmost Bliss. In the northeast, in the Buddha-land of Store of Treasures, ninety koṭis of non-retrogressing bodhisattvas shall be born in the Western Land of Utmost Bliss. From the Buddha-lands of Immeasurable Sound, of Light, of Dragon Gods, of Victorious Power, of the Lion, of Freedom from Dust, of Foremost Virtue, of the Humane King, and of Flower Banner, the non-retrogressing bodhisattvas who shall attain rebirth number some tens or hundreds of koṭis, some hundreds of thousands of koṭis, even unto ten thousand koṭis.
The above briefly names the Buddha-lands of eleven other directions and the numbers of bodhisattvas who attain rebirth there.

[The twelfth Buddha is named Supreme Flower. He has countless multitudes of bodhisattvas, all non-retrogressing. In wisdom and courage they have already made offerings to immeasurable Buddhas, are possessed of great diligence, and have set their course upon the One Vehicle. Within seven days they can gather in the firm dharmas cultivated by great beings throughout a hundred thousand koṭis of kalpas. Bodhisattvas such as these shall all attain rebirth.]

The twelfth Buddha is named Supreme Flower. He has countless multitudes of bodhisattvas, all at the stage of non-retrogression. In wisdom and courage they have already made offerings to immeasurable Buddhas, are possessed of great diligence, and have made vows setting their course upon the One Vehicle (ultimate Buddhahood). Within seven days they can gather in the firm dharmas cultivated by great beings throughout a hundred thousand koṭis of kalpas. Bodhisattvas such as these shall all attain rebirth in the Western Land of Utmost Bliss.

[The thirteenth Buddha is named Fearless. He has seven hundred and ninety koṭis of great bodhisattvas, and bodhisattvas of small practice and bhikshus beyond all reckoning, all of whom shall attain rebirth. As for the Buddhas' names throughout the worlds of the ten directions and the multitudes of bodhisattvas who shall attain rebirth, were one to speak only their names, kalpas would not suffice to exhaust them.]

The thirteenth Buddha is named Fearless. He has seven hundred and ninety koṭis of great bodhisattvas, and bodhisattvas of small practice and multitudes of bhikshus beyond reckoning, all of whom shall attain rebirth in the Western Land of Utmost Bliss. As for the Buddhas' names throughout the worlds of the ten directions and their multitudes of bodhisattvas who shall attain rebirth in the Western Land of Utmost Bliss, were one to speak only their names, kalpas would not suffice to exhaust them.

[The Buddha said to the Kind One: You see those bodhisattva-mahasattvas who have well obtained benefit. If there are good men and good women who hear the name of Amitābha Buddha and can give rise to a single thought of joyful love, take refuge, look up in reverence,
and practice as taught

, you should know that such persons obtain great benefit and shall gain the merits spoken of above. Their minds are neither base nor arrogant, and the roots of virtue they accomplish all increase. You should know that such persons are not of the Lesser Vehicle; in my Dharma they are called foremost disciples.]

The Buddha said to Bodhisattva Maitreya: You see those great bodhisattvas who are born in the Western Land of Utmost Bliss and have well obtained benefit. If there are good men and good women who hear the name of Amitābha Buddha and can give rise to a single thought of joyful love, take refuge, look up in reverence, and practice as taught, you should know that such persons obtain great benefit and shall gain the merits spoken of above. Their minds are neither base nor arrogant, and the roots of virtue they accomplish all grow ever upward. You should know that such persons are not of the Lesser Vehicle; in my Dharma they are called foremost disciples.

[Well obtaining benefit] Those of the supreme grade of the supreme class see the Buddha, hear the Dharma, and at once awaken to the unborn, ascending to the eighth ground. Hence it is said, “they well obtain benefit.”
The Sutra of Contemplation on the Buddha of Immeasurable Life says:

“At the time of being born in that land, because this person is diligent and courageous, Amitābha Tathagata, together with Avalokitesvara and Mahasthamaprapta and countless transformation Buddhas, hundreds of thousands of bhikshus and multitudes of sravakas, and immeasurable gods, and seven-jewel palaces, come before the practitioner, with Bodhisattva Avalokitesvara bearing a vajra throne and Bodhisattva Mahasthamaprapta beside him. Amitābha Buddha sends forth a great radiance that illumines the practitioner's body, and with all the bodhisattvas extends his hand in welcome. Avalokitesvara, Mahasthamaprapta, and countless bodhisattvas praise the practitioner and encourage his mind. When the practitioner sees this, he is joyful and exultant, and sees his own body riding upon the vajra throne, following behind the Buddha, and in the time of a finger-snap he is born in that land. Having been born in that land, he sees the Buddha's bodily form complete in all marks, and sees the bodhisattvas complete in their bodily marks, and the radiant jewel-groves proclaiming the wondrous Dharma. Having heard it,
he at once awakens to the patient acceptance of the unborn

, and in the space of a moment he journeys to serve all the Buddhas throughout the ten directions, and before each Buddha receives his prophecy in turn. Returning to his own land, he gains immeasurable hundreds of thousands of dharanis. This is called the supreme grade of the supreme class.”

[The eighth ground] The eighth of the bodhisattva's ten grounds, named the Immovable Ground. In this ground the bodhisattva abides in the patience of the unborn, cuts off all deliberate effort, and his body and mind are still and extinguished, like empty space; he accomplishes the perfection of vow and, with the mind of nirvāṇa, is serene and unmoving, and so it is named the “Immovable Ground.” [The ten grounds] Among the fifty-two stages of the bodhisattva's practice, the fifth set of ten is called the ten grounds. Within these ten grounds one gradually opens the Buddha-realm and accomplishes the wisdom of all modes, already belonging to the sage's stage, and so they are also called the “ten sages.”

[Therefore I tell you, gods, humans, asuras, and all the rest of the world: you should delight in and cultivate this, and give rise to a rare heart. In this sutra, give rise to the thought of a guiding teacher. Those who wish to cause immeasurable sentient beings swiftly to abide and attain non-retrogression, and who wish to see that vast and majestic, supremely receptive Buddha-land and to perfect its merits, should rouse diligence and listen to this Dharma-gate.]

Therefore, I tell you gods, humans, asuras, and all the rest: you should delight in and cultivate the Pure Land Dharma-gate, and give rise to a rare heart. In this sutra, give rise to the thought of a guiding teacher. Those who wish to cause immeasurable sentient beings swiftly to abide and attain non-retrogression, and who wish to see that vast and majestic, supremely receptive Buddha-land and to perfect its merits, should rouse diligence and listen to and receive this Pure Land Dharma-gate.
[In this sutra, give rise to the thought of a guiding teacher] Through what this sutra teaches one can give rise to genuine faith and practice as taught.

[For the sake of seeking the Dharma, do not give rise to a mind of retreat or cowardice, or of flattery and deceit. Even were you to enter a great fire, you should not doubt or regret. Why is that? Because those immeasurable koṭis of bodhisattvas all seek this subtle and wondrous Dharma-gate, listening to it with reverence and giving rise to no opposition. There are many bodhisattvas who wish to hear this sutra but cannot obtain it. Therefore you should seek this Dharma.]

For the sake of seeking the Dharma, do not give rise to a mind of retreat or cowardice, or of flattery and deceit. Even were you to enter a great fire, you should not doubt or regret. Why is that? Because those immeasurable koṭis of bodhisattvas all seek this subtle and wondrous Pure Land Dharma-gate, listening to it with reverence and giving rise to no opposition. There are many bodhisattvas who wish to hear this sutra but cannot obtain it. Therefore you should ardently seek this Pure Land Dharma-gate.

[If in future ages, even down to the time when the True Dharma is extinguished, there are sentient beings who plant all roots of goodness and have already made offerings to immeasurable Buddhas, then through the added power of those Tathagatas they can obtain this vast and great Dharma-gate, receive and uphold it, and shall attain the vast wisdom of all wisdom. In that Dharma they shall gain vast and profound understanding and obtain great joy. They shall proclaim it widely to others and always delight in its practice.]

If in future ages, even down to the time when the True Dharma is extinguished, there are sentient beings who plant all roots of goodness and have already made offerings to immeasurable Buddhas, then, receiving the majestic spiritual power and added protection of Amitābha Buddha, they can obtain this vast and great Dharma-gate (the Pure Land Dharma-gate), receive and uphold it, and shall attain the vast wisdom of all wisdom. In that Dharma they shall gain vast and profound understanding and obtain great joy. They shall proclaim it widely to others and always delight in its practice.

[The vast and great Dharma-gate] In the age of the Final Dharma, though a hundred million times a hundred million people cultivate, hardly one attains the Way; only by relying on reciting the Buddha's name can one cross birth and death. Therefore the Pure Land Dharma-gate is the Dharma-gate that delivers sentient beings broadly, and so it is called the “vast and great Dharma-gate.” [The wisdom of all wisdom] The wisdom within all wisdom; that is, the Buddha's wisdom.

[Good men and good women who can, with regard to this Dharma, whether they have sought it, now seek it, or shall seek it, all obtain good benefit. You should abide in it without doubt, plant all roots of goodness, and constantly cultivate, so that you have no doubt or stagnation and do not enter the prison of every kind of treasure and attainment.]

Good men and good women who can, with regard to this Dharma (the Pure Land Dharma-gate), whether they have sought it, now seek it, or shall seek it, all obtain good benefit. You should abide in it without doubt, plant all roots of goodness, and constantly cultivate, so that you have no doubt or stagnation and do not enter the prison of every kind of wealth and attainment.

[Ajita, beings of great majesty and virtue such as these can give rise to the vast and extraordinary gates of the Buddha-Dharma. Because they do not hear this Dharma, there are a hundred million bodhisattvas who fall back from anuttara-samyak-sambodhi.]

Maitreya, beings of great majesty and virtue such as these (those who can, with regard to this Dharma, whether they have sought it, now seek it, or shall seek it) can give rise to faith in the vast and extraordinary skillful-means Dharma-gate of the Buddha-Dharma. Because this Dharma-gate is not heard, there are a hundred million bodhisattvas who fall back from anuttara-samyak-sambodhi.

[The extraordinary skillful-means Dharma-gate] The Pure Land Dharma-gate is the most skillful of skillful means and the shortest of shortcuts, and so it is the extraordinary skillful-means Dharma-gate.

[If there are sentient beings who copy this sutra, make offerings to it, receive and uphold it, read and recite it; who for even a moment expound it to others and encourage them to listen; who give rise to no worry or affliction, and even day and night contemplate that land and the Buddha's merits — they shall never fall back from the unsurpassed Way.]

If there are sentient beings who copy this sutra, make offerings to it, receive and uphold it, read and recite it; who for even a moment expound it to others and encourage them to listen; who give rise to no worry or affliction, and even day and night contemplate the Western Land of Utmost Bliss and the merits of Amitābha Buddha — they shall never fall back from the unsurpassed Way (the Way of Buddhahood).

[At such a person's death, even if the three-thousand-great-thousand world were filled with a great fire, he can transcend it and be born in that land. Such a person has already met the Buddhas of the past and received the prophecy of bodhi. All Tathagatas together praise him. Therefore you should single-mindedly believe and accept, uphold, recite, proclaim, and practice it.]

At their death, even if the three-thousand-great-thousand world were filled with a great fire, they can transcend it and be born in the Western Land of Utmost Bliss. Such persons have already met the Buddhas of the past and received the prophecy of bodhi (the prophecy that they shall certainly become Buddhas in the future). All Tathagatas together praise them. Therefore you should single-mindedly believe and accept this sutra, and uphold, recite, proclaim, and practice it (practice as taught).

[Now I, for the sake of all sentient beings, proclaim this sutra and its Dharma, causing them to behold Amitābha Buddha and all that belongs to his land. Whatever should be done, all of it may be sought therein. Do not, after my entry into nirvāṇa, give rise to doubt again.]

Now, for the sake of all sentient beings, I proclaim this sutra and its Dharma, causing them to behold Amitābha Buddha and all that belongs to his land. Whatever should be done (that is, the faith, the vows, and the practice by which one seeks birth in the Western Land of Utmost Bliss) must be striven after with all one's might. You must not, after my entry into nirvāṇa, give rise to doubt again.

[In ages to come, the scriptures and the Way will be utterly extinguished. Out of compassion and pity, I will specially preserve this sutra, to remain for a hundred years. Whatever sentient beings encounter this sutra will, according to their own wishes, all attain deliverance.]

In ages to come, the scriptures and the Way will be utterly extinguished. Out of compassion and pity, I will specially preserve this sutra, to abide for a hundred years more. Whatever sentient beings encounter this sutra will, according to their own wishes, all attain deliverance.
[The extinction of the scriptures and the Way] The Jingying Commentary says:

“In ages to come, when the scriptures and the Way are extinguished — this sets forth the matter of the Dharma's extinction in the future. Śākyamuni's True Dharma lasts five hundred years, the Semblance Dharma a thousand years, and the Final Dharma ten thousand years. When all of these have passed, it is called complete extinction.”
Master Shandao's Verses of Praise for Rebirth says:
“When the Three Jewels are extinguished after ten thousand years, this sutra remains for a hundred years.”

[True Dharma, Semblance Dharma, Final Dharma] The Buddha-Dharma is divided into three periods: the period of the True Dharma, the period of the Semblance Dharma, and the period of the Final Dharma. In the period of the True Dharma, although the Buddha has entered nirvāṇa, the Dharma and its forms are unchanged: there is teaching, there is practice, and there are those who realize the fruit — this is called the period of the True Dharma. In the period of the Semblance Dharma, semblance means likeness: it resembles the True Dharma but is not the True Dharma. In this period there is teaching and there is practice, but those who realize the fruit are already very few. In the period of the Final Dharma, final means feeble: this period declines into feebleness, and there is only teaching without practice, and no one at all who realizes the fruit.

[For a Tathagata to appear in the world is hard to meet and hard to see. The scriptures and the Way of the Buddhas are hard to obtain and hard to hear. To meet a good spiritual friend and, having heard the Dharma, be able to practice it — this too is difficult. If one hears this sutra and believes, delights in, and upholds it, of all difficulties there is none that surpasses this.]

For a Tathagata to appear in the world is hard to meet and hard to see. The scriptures and the Way of the Buddhas are hard to obtain and hard to hear. To meet a good spiritual friend and, having heard the Dharma, be able to practice it — this too is difficult. If one hears this sutra and believes, delights in, and upholds it, of all difficulties there is none that surpasses this.

[If there are sentient beings who, hearing the Buddha's name, have a pure and compassionate mind, leap up with joy, feel the hairs of their bodies stand on end, or shed tears, it is all because in past lives they cultivated the Buddha-way; therefore they are not ordinary people.]

If there are sentient beings who, hearing the name of Amitābha Buddha, have a pure and compassionate mind, leap up with joy, feel the hairs of their bodies stand on end, or shed tears, it is all because in past lives they cultivated the Buddha-way; therefore they are not ordinary people.
[Hearing the Buddha's name] That is, hearing the name of Amitābha Buddha.
The Sutra of Immeasurable Life as Spoken by the Buddha (the Wei translation) has
“having heard the name of that Buddha”
and the Assembly of the Tathagata of Immeasurable Life (the Tang translation) has
“hearing the name of that Buddha”
and the Sutra of the Adornment of Immeasurable Life, the Great Vehicle, as Spoken by the Buddha (the Song translation) has
“having heard the name of the Buddha of Immeasurable Life”

[If, hearing the Buddha's name, one is dubious in mind and, with regard to the Buddha's scriptural words, believes nothing at all, such persons have all come from the evil paths; their past calamity is not yet exhausted, and they are not yet to be delivered. Hence their minds are dubious and they do not believe and turn toward it.]

If, hearing the name of Amitābha Buddha, one is dubious in mind and, with regard to the Buddha's scriptural words, believes nothing at all, such persons have all come from the evil paths; their past calamity is not yet exhausted, and they are not yet to be delivered. Hence their minds are dubious and they cannot believe and accept it.

[The Buddha told Maitreya: The unsurpassed Dharma of the Buddhas and Tathagatas — the deeply profound Dharma of the ten powers, the fearlessnesses, the unobstructed, and the unattached, and the bodhisattva Dharmas such as the pāramitās — is not easily encountered. Those able to expound the Dharma also find it hard to reveal. Those of firm and deep faith are, again, rarely to be met.]

The Buddha told Bodhisattva Maitreya: The unsurpassed Dharma of the Buddhas and Tathagatas — the deeply profound Dharma of the ten powers, the fearlessnesses, the unobstructed, and the unattached, and the bodhisattva Dharmas such as the pāramitās — is by no means easy to encounter. Those able to expound the Dharma also find it hard to reveal. Those of firm and deep faith, likewise, are not easy to find.

[Now I proclaim in accordance with principle this vast and subtle Dharma-gate, which is praised by all Buddhas. I entrust it to you, that you may make great protection for it, for the benefit of all sentient beings throughout the long night. Do not let sentient beings sink and fall into the five destinies, to suffer every kind of peril and pain.]

Now I proclaim in accordance with principle this vast and subtle Pure Land Dharma-gate, which is praised by all Buddhas. I entrust it to you, that you may make great protection for it, so as to benefit all sentient beings throughout the long night. Do not let them sink and fall into the five destinies, to suffer every kind of peril and pain.
[I entrust it to you]

Bodhisattva Maitreya is a bodhisattva with but one life remaining, who presently dwells in the Inner Court of the Tuṣita Heaven. After four thousand years (that is, five billion six hundred seventy million years in human reckoning), he will descend and be born in the human world, and beneath the dragon-flower tree in the Hua-lin Grove he will realize Buddhahood; following after Śākyamuni Buddha, he is the fifth Tathagata of the Worthy Kalpa.
“The Buddha told Maitreya:

Now I proclaim in accordance with principle this vast and subtle Dharma-gate, which is praised by all Buddhas. I entrust it to you, that you may make great protection for it, for the benefit of all sentient beings throughout the long night.”
This shows that after Bodhisattva Maitreya realizes Buddhahood in this Sahā world, he too will proclaim and spread the Sutra of Immeasurable Life.
[The long night] A simile for the long darkness of ignorance through which ordinary beings, from beginningless kalpas, transmigrate in birth and death.

[You should diligently cultivate practice and comply with my teaching. You should be filial to the Buddha and constantly remember the kindness of the teacher. You should cause this Dharma to abide long and not be extinguished. You should steadfastly uphold it, and not destroy or lose it. You must not, out of delusion, add to or subtract from the sutra-Dharma.]

You should diligently cultivate practice and comply with my teaching. You should be filial to the Buddha and constantly remember the kindness of the original teacher. You should cause this Dharma to abide long and not be extinguished. You should steadfastly uphold it, and not destroy or lose it. You must not recklessly add to or subtract from the sutra-Dharma.

[If you are mindful without cease, you will attain the Way swiftly. My Dharma is thus; thus do I speak. The practice of the Tathagata you too should follow. Cultivate merit and goodness, and seek birth in the Pure Land.]

For one who is mindful of the name of Amitābha Buddha without cease, thought following thought, the Way is swiftly attained. My Dharma is thus; thus do I speak. The practice of the Tathagata you too should follow. Cultivate merit and goodness, and seek birth in the Western Land of Utmost Bliss.
[Mindful without cease] “Constantly mindful” means constantly mindful of the name of Amitābha Buddha; “without cease” means thought following thought without interruption.

blocks.text: 47. The Fortunate and Wise First Hear It

inline.s: [At that time the World-Honored One spoke in verse, saying:
Then the World-Honored One spoke these verses:
Had you not in former lives cultivated merit and wisdom,
you could not hear
(you would not hear the Pure Land Dharma-gate, or, having heard it, you would be unable to give rise to faith and take it in)
this true Dharma; but having once made offerings to the Tathagatas, you can joyfully believe in this matter.
The evil, the proud, the indolent, and those of wrong views find it hard to believe the Tathagata's subtle Dharma; like the blind who forever dwell in darkness, they cannot guide others on the road.
Only if in former lives one served the Buddhas and planted every root of goodness can one cultivate this world-saving deed
(the Pure Land Dharma-gate);
having heard it, one upholds and copies it, recites it, praises and expounds it, and makes offerings.
[The world-saving deed] The Pure Land Dharma-gate can broadly deliver sentient beings from birth and death, and so it is called “the world-saving deed.”

If thus with one mind you seek the pure land, you will surely be born in the Land of Utmost Bliss; though a great fire filled the three thousand worlds, riding the Buddha's majestic power you would transcend it all.

The Tathagata's deep and vast ocean of wisdom only Buddhas with Buddhas can know; śrāvakas for koṭis of kalpas pondering the Buddha's wisdom, though they exhaust their spiritual powers, cannot fathom it.
The Tathagata's merits the Buddha knows of himself; only the World-Honored One can reveal them. A human body is hard to gain, a Buddha is hard to meet
(hard to encounter),
and to hear the Dharma with faith and wisdom is the hardest of the hard.

If all sentient beings are to become Buddhas, their practice must surpass Samantabhadra's, and they must ascend to the other shore; therefore you learned and wise ones of broad knowledge should believe my teaching, and receive it as the truth I speak.

Having been so fortunate as to hear this wondrous Dharma, you should constantly recollect the Buddha and give rise to joy; upholding it, broadly cross the stream of birth and death — the Buddha says that such a one is a true good friend.]

[Upholding it and broadly crossing the stream of birth and death] To receive and uphold this sutra and, by this Pure Land Dharma-gate, to broaden and deliver those sentient beings who are drowning in birth and death. “Zhi liu” — “those of such a kind” — means a certain person or thing of one and the same class. “The stream of birth and death” is the current of birth and death, that is, the sentient beings who are drowning in birth and death. [The Buddha says that such a one is a true good friend] The Buddha says that such a person is truly a good friend of sentient beings (a good spiritual friend).

blocks.text: 48. The Benefits of Hearing the Sutra

inline.s: [At that time, when the World-Honored One had spoken this sutra and its Dharma, in the heavens and the human world there were twelve thousand nayuta koṭis of sentient beings who, far from dust and defilement, attained the pure Dharma-eye. Twenty koṭis of sentient beings attained the fruit of Anāgāmin. Six thousand eight hundred bhikṣus, their outflows all exhausted, attained liberation of mind. Forty koṭis of bodhisattvas abided in non-retrogression from the unsurpassed bodhi, adorning themselves with the merit of their great vows. Twenty-five koṭis of sentient beings attained the patience of non-retrogression. Four koṭi-koṭis of hundreds of thousands of sentient beings, who had never before given rise to the intention of unsurpassed bodhi, now for the first time gave rise to it. Planting all roots of goodness and vowing to be born in the Land of Utmost Bliss and to see Amitābha Buddha, they will all be reborn in that Tathagata's land. Each in a different region, they will in turn become Buddhas, all of the same name, the Tathagata Wonderful Sound.]

At that time, when the World-Honored One had finished speaking this sutra and its Dharma, in the heavens and the human world there were twelve thousand times ten thousand million sentient beings who, far from dust and defilement
(affliction)

, attained the pure Dharma-eye. Twenty koṭis of sentient beings attained the fruit of Anāgāmin. Six thousand eight hundred bhikṣus, their afflictions all exhausted, attained liberation of mind. Forty koṭis of bodhisattvas abided in non-retrogression from the unsurpassed bodhi, adorning themselves with the merit of their great vows. Twenty-five koṭis of sentient beings attained the patience of non-retrogression. Four koṭi-koṭis of hundreds of thousands of sentient beings, who had never before given rise to the intention of unsurpassed bodhi, now for the first time gave rise to it. They planted all roots of goodness and, vowing to be born in the Land of Utmost Bliss and to see Amitābha Buddha, will all be reborn in the Western Land of Utmost Bliss. Each in a different region of the ten directions, they will in turn become Buddhas, all of the same name, the Tathagata Wonderful Sound.
[Their afflictions all exhausted] They attained the fruit of Arhatship.

[Furthermore, in the Buddha-lands of the ten directions, whether those now being born or those to be born in the future who see Amitābha Buddha — in each case there are eighty thousand koṭi nayuta persons who attain the prophecy and the Dharma-patience, and accomplish the unsurpassed bodhi. Those sentient beings, all through the karmic conditions of Amitābha Buddha's past vows, alike attain rebirth in the Western Land of Utmost Bliss.]

Furthermore, in the Buddha-lands of the ten directions, whether those now being born or those to be born in the future who see Amitābha Buddha — in each case there are eighty thousand times ten thousand million persons who attain the prophecy and win the patience of the non-arising of dharmas, and accomplish the unsurpassed bodhi (perfectly realizing the Buddha-fruit). These sentient beings, all through the karmic conditions of Amitābha Buddha's past vows, alike attain rebirth in the Western Land of Utmost Bliss.
[Koṭi] A unit of number used in ancient India, equivalent to what is now called a hundred million.

[At that time the three-thousand-great-thousand world trembled in six ways and manifested all manner of rare and miraculous transformations, emitting a great light that universally illumined the ten directions. Furthermore, the gods in the heavens played wondrous music and uttered sounds of rejoicing. Even all the gods of the form realm heard it, and exclaimed that such a thing had never been. Measureless wondrous flowers came raining down in profusion.]

At that time the three-thousand-great-thousand world trembled in six ways and manifested all manner of rare and miraculous transformations, emitting a great light that universally illumined the ten directions. Furthermore, the gods in the heavens played wondrous music and uttered sounds of rejoicing. Even all the gods of the form realm heard it, and exclaimed that such a thing had never been. Measureless wondrous flowers came raining down in profusion.

[The Venerable Ānanda, Bodhisattva Maitreya, and all the bodhisattvas and śrāvakas, the gods, nāgas, and the eight classes of beings, the whole great assembly, hearing what the Buddha had spoken, all rejoiced greatly, believed and accepted it, and practiced it in accordance.]

The Venerable Ānanda, Bodhisattva Maitreya, and all the bodhisattvas and śrāvakas, the gods, nāgas, and the eight classes of beings, the whole great assembly, hearing what the Buddha had spoken, all rejoiced greatly, believed and accepted it, and practiced it in accordance.
